MAIN.title: About me
MAIN.description:
I am a computer science graduate with hands-on experience in mobile, web, backend, and database systems development.
In my free time I like developing my own hobby projects to learn new technologies. I am particularly interested in writing Google extensions and mobile applications.

CLAIMER.title: Free Game Claimer
CLAIMER.meta_title: Free Game Claimer: auto claim free Epic, Steam, GOG & Prime games
CLAIMER.meta_description: Free browser extension that claims free games from Epic Games, Steam, GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming automatically, using your existing logged-in sessions. Open source, for Chrome and Firefox.
CLAIMER.tagline: Claim free games from Epic, Steam, GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming automatically
CLAIMER.intro: Free Game Claimer is a free, open source browser extension for Chrome and Firefox. It checks the stores for free games on a schedule you choose and claims them for you, so you never have to remember giveaway day.
CLAIMER.promo_alt: Free Game Claimer popup showing the settings tab and the list of free games
CLAIMER.feature1: Five stores: Epic Games, Steam, GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming. Epic and Steam are on by default, the other three you switch on yourself.
CLAIMER.feature2: Automatic checks: on browser start, every hour, every 6 hours, every 12 hours or once a day (the default). For the daily check you can also pick the hour.
CLAIMER.feature3: Manual claim: one button claims whatever is free right now.
CLAIMER.feature4: Free games list: every currently free game from the stores you enabled, plus upcoming Epic free games, with a filter by store.
CLAIMER.feature5: Claimed counter: see how many games the extension has claimed for you.
CLAIMER.feature6: Steam review filter: only claim Steam games with at least the share of positive reviews you set, or pick a Steam rating preset.
CLAIMER.feature7: Prime Gaming offers: choose which kinds of Prime offers to claim (Amazon Games App, Epic-linked, GOG-linked, Windows-linked or Legacy Games). It needs an Amazon account with Prime.
CLAIMER.feature8: IndieGala Wheel of Fortune: optionally spins IndieGala's wheel for you.
CLAIMER.feature9: Status at a glance: the popup shows whether you are logged in to each store and warns you when a store has changed or a captcha needs you.
CLAIMER.privacy1: The extension works inside your browser, with the sessions you are already logged in with on each store. It never asks for your store passwords and does not store them.
CLAIMER.privacy2: To claim a game it opens the store page like you would. If a store shows a captcha or a login page it cannot get past, it leaves that tab for you to finish.
CLAIMER.privacy3: Epic and Steam work out of the box. GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming need extra site access, which your browser asks you to approve when you switch each one on.
CLAIMER.privacy4: There is no Free Game Claimer account or server. Your settings and the game lists stay in your browser's extension storage; the extension only talks to the stores. If you use Legacy Games offers you can enter an email for the codes, which is stored the same way.
CLAIMER.privacy5: It is free, without ads or paid features, and open source under the MIT licence. Read the code on GitHub.
CLAIMER.q1: Is Free Game Claimer really free?
CLAIMER.a1: Yes. It has no ads, no paid tier and no premium features, and the code is open source under the MIT licence. If it saves you money, you can support it on the donate page, but you never have to.
CLAIMER.a2: No. It uses the sessions you are already logged in with in your browser, and it never asks for or stores your store passwords. If you are logged out of a store, the popup shows a Log in link instead.
CLAIMER.a3: Epic Games, Steam, GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming. Prime Gaming offers need an Amazon account with a Prime membership.
CLAIMER.q4: How often does it check for free games?
CLAIMER.a4: You choose: on browser start, every hour, every 6 hours, every 12 hours or once a day, which is the default. For the daily check you can pick an hour; if your browser is closed then, it runs when you next open it that day. The Manually claim button checks right away.
CLAIMER.q5: Does it work during Epic's holiday mystery games giveaway?
CLAIMER.a5: The extension reads Epic's own free games list on your schedule and tries to claim every game that list shows as free, and upcoming Epic free games appear in its Free Games tab. It has no special handling for the mystery games, so I cannot promise how Epic lists each mystery offer or that every one gets claimed. If one is missed, press Manually claim or claim it on Epic's page.
CLAIMER.a6: Yes. There is a Firefox version on Mozilla Add-ons (Firefox 113 or newer) as well as the Chrome version on the Chrome Web Store.
CLAIMER.faq_bug: A store changed and something stopped working?
